summary: 1. **July 7 ore beat its target for the first time in July** — 5,053 BCM against a 1,822 BCM target (+3,231 BCM), while total production missed (−4.8%) and waste ran well under target. 2. Two ore blocks contributed for the first time this month (735-178-1 and 770-164-2). 3. EX-123 stayed down a second full day on its track fault. 4. MTD ore gap narrowed sharply (−14.2%, from −31.6% the day before). 5. Survey posted a clean +9.4% recovery from Day 12's −44.9% reversal (MTD +6.0%). 6. Drill Rig daily availability fell sharply (81.51%, from 97.14%) on a new DR-139 breakdown ("hard braking"), distinct from the standing DR-125 pattern; a new "lack of drilling area" standby theme appeared on three rigs. 7. **The Week 28-29 bi-weekly plan deck landed with the pass's most consequential finding: DR-124, DR-125, and DR-139 are all planned at 0% availability for the entire Week 28 window** — very likely the real explanation for DR-125's seven-straight-day "lack of operator" standby reading, reframing what had been an open staffing question into a probable planning artifact. 8. EX-263 is separately written out at 0% PA for Week 29, repeating the W24-25 pattern.
